sanskrit: indhā̍no a̱gniṁ va̍navad vanuṣya̱taḥ kṛ̱tabra̍hmā śūśuvad rā̱taha̍vya̱ it | jā̱tena̍ jā̱tam ati̱ sa pra sa̍rsṛte̱ yaṁ-ya̱ṁ yuja̍ṁ kṛṇu̱te brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍ḥ ||
english: Kindling Agni, he shall conquer the foes who wish him ill; he who has wrought the sacred hymn, who has offered the oblation, shall flourish exceedingly. Born after born he overruns and surpasses them — whomsoever Brahmaṇaspati takes as his companion.

sanskrit: vī̱rebhi̍r vī̱rān va̍navad vanuṣya̱to gobhī̍ ra̱yim pa̍pratha̱d bodha̍ti̱ tmanā̍ | to̱kaṁ ca̱ tasya̱ tana̍yaṁ ca vardhate̱ yaṁ-ya̱ṁ yuja̍ṁ kṛṇu̱te brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍ḥ ||
english: With heroes he shall conquer the hostile heroes; with kine he has spread wealth wide and is himself awake. His offspring and his progeny both grow and thrive — whomsoever Brahmaṇaspati takes as his companion.

sanskrit: sindhu̱r na kṣoda̱ḥ śimī̍vām̐ ṛghāya̱to vṛṣe̍va̱ vadhrī̍m̐r a̱bhi va̱ṣṭy oja̍sā | a̱gner i̍va̱ prasi̍ti̱r nāha̱ varta̍ve̱ yaṁ-ya̱ṁ yuja̍ṁ kṛṇu̱te brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍ḥ ||
english: Like a rushing river, mighty, he overwhelms those who rage against him; like a bull he overpowers the weaklings with his might. Like the onrush of Agni there is no turning it back — whomsoever Brahmaṇaspati takes as his companion.

sanskrit: tasmā̍ arṣanti di̱vyā a̍sa̱ścata̱ḥ sa satva̍bhiḥ pratha̱mo goṣu̍ gacchati | ani̍bhṛṣṭataviṣir ha̱nty oja̍sā̱ yaṁ-ya̱ṁ yuja̍ṁ kṛṇu̱te brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍ḥ ||
english: For him the heavenly, inexhaustible ones stream forth; he with his warriors goes foremost among the cows. His force undiminished, he slays with might — whomsoever Brahmaṇaspati takes as his companion.

sanskrit: tasmā̱ id viśve̍ dhunayanta̱ sindha̱vo 'cchi̍drā̱ śarma̍ dadhire pu̱rūṇi̍ | de̱vānā̍ṁ su̱mne su̱bhaga̱ḥ sa e̍dhate̱ yaṁ-ya̱ṁ yuja̍ṁ kṛṇu̱te brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍ḥ ||
english: All rivers rush resoundingly for him; unbroken, they have bestowed many shelters upon him. In the goodwill of the gods he prospers, the blessed one — whomsoever Brahmaṇaspati takes as his companion.

sanskrit: ṛ̱jur ic chaṁso̍ vanavad vanuṣya̱to de̍va̱yann id ade̍vayantam a̱bhy a̍sat | su̱prā̱vīr id va̍navat pṛ̱tsu du̱ṣṭara̱ṁ yajved aya̍jyo̱r vi bha̍jāti̱ bhoja̍nam ||
english: Truly the honest worshipper shall conquer those who wish him ill; he who is devout shall prevail over the impious. He who is well-equipped shall win in battles the hard-to-conquer; he who sacrifices distributes the enjoyment from the non-sacrificer.

sanskrit: yaja̍sva vīra̱ pra vi̍hi manāya̱to bha̱dram mana̍ḥ kṛṇuṣva vṛtra̱tūrye̍ | ha̱viṣ kṛ̍ṇuṣva su̱bhago̱ yathāsa̍si̱ brahma̍ṇa̱s pate̱r ava̱ ā vṛ̍ṇīmahe ||
english: Sacrifice, O hero; send forth to those who are devoted; make your mind auspicious in the conquest of Vṛtra. Prepare the oblation so that you may be blessed — we choose the grace of Brahmaṇaspati for ourselves.

sanskrit: sa ij jane̍na̱ sa vi̱śā sa janma̍nā̱ sa pu̱trair vāja̍m bharate̱ dhanā̱ nṛbhi̍ḥ | de̱vānā̱ṁ yaḥ pi̱tara̍m ā̱vivā̍sati śra̱ddhāma̍nā ha̱viṣā̱ brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍m ||
english: He indeed with his folk, with his clan, with his kindred, with his sons, bears off the prize-booty and wealth with his men — he who with devoted heart and oblation seeks to please Brahmaṇaspati, father of the gods.

sanskrit: yo a̍smai ha̱vyair ghṛ̱tava̍dbhi̱r avi̍dha̱t pra tam prā̱cā na̍yati̱ brahma̍ṇa̱s pati̍ḥ | u̱ru̱ṣyatī̱m aṁha̍so̱ rakṣa̍tī ri̱ṣo̱3̱̍ 'ṁhoś ci̍d asmā uru̱cakri̱r adbhu̍taḥ ||
english: Him who has attended Brahmaṇaspati with fat-laden oblations, Brahmaṇaspati leads forward on the eastern path. He guards from distress, protects from injury — the wide-acting, wondrous one saves him even from the narrowest strait.

sanskrit: i̱mā gira̍ ādi̱tyebhyo̍ ghṛ̱tasnū̍ḥ sa̱nād rāja̍bhyo ju̱hvā̍ juhomi | śṛ̱ṇotu̍ mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā bhago̍ nas tuvijā̱to varu̍ṇo̱ dakṣo̱ aṁśa̍ḥ ||
english: These hymns, flowing like ghee, I offer with my tongue as an oblation to the Ādityas, the eternal kings. May Mitra, Aryaman, Bhaga hear us, may Varuṇa of mighty birth, Dakṣa, and Aṁśa hear.

sanskrit: i̱maṁ stoma̱ṁ sakra̍tavo me a̱dya mi̱tro a̍rya̱mā varu̍ṇo juṣanta | ā̱di̱tyāsa̱ḥ śuca̍yo̱ dhāra̍pūtā̱ avṛ̍jinā anava̱dyā ari̍ṣṭāḥ ||
english: May Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa, of one purpose with me, accept this hymn of praise today. The Ādityas, pure, cleansed by the stream of truth, faultless, blameless, inviolate.

sanskrit: ta ā̍di̱tyāsa̍ u̱ravo̍ gabhī̱rā ada̍bdhāso̱ dipsa̍nto bhūrya̱kṣāḥ | a̱ntaḥ pa̍śyanti vṛji̱nota sā̱dhu sarva̱ṁ rāja̍bhyaḥ para̱mā ci̱d anti̍ ||
english: Those Ādityas are broad and deep, undeceived, warding off deceit, with many eyes. They see within both the crooked and the straight — all things are near even to these kings from the farthest distance.

sanskrit: dhā̱raya̍nta ādi̱tyāso̱ jaga̱t sthā de̱vā viśva̍sya̱ bhuva̍nasya go̱pāḥ | dī̱rghādhi̍yo̱ rakṣa̍māṇā asu̱rya̍m ṛ̱tāvā̍na̱ś caya̍mānā ṛ̱ṇāni̍ ||
english: The Ādityas sustain the moving and the standing; they are gods, guardians of all the world. Of far-reaching wisdom, protecting their divine lordship, upholders of ṛta, exacting the dues owed them.

sanskrit: vi̱dyām ā̍dityā̱ ava̍so vo a̱sya yad a̍ryaman bha̱ya ā ci̍n mayo̱bhu | yu̱ṣmāka̍m mitrāvaruṇā̱ praṇī̍tau̱ pari̱ śvabhre̍va duri̱tāni̍ vṛjyām ||
english: O Ādityas, may we know your aid in this matter — O Aryaman, even from fear there is comfort. Under your guidance, O Mitra and Varuṇa, may I turn aside all evils as around a pit.

sanskrit: su̱go hi vo̍ aryaman mitra̱ panthā̍ anṛkṣa̱ro va̍ruṇa sā̱dhur asti̍ | tenā̍dityā̱ adhi̍ vocatā no̱ yaccha̍tā no duṣpari̱hantu̱ śarma̍ ||
english: For easy is your path, O Aryaman, free of thorns, O Mitra; it is well-made, O Varuṇa. By that path, O Ādityas, speak favorably for us; grant us shelter hard for the wicked to assail.

sanskrit: pipa̍rtu no̱ adi̍tī̱ rāja̍pu̱trāti̱ dveṣā̍ṁsy arya̱mā su̱gebhi̍ḥ | bṛ̱han mi̱trasya̱ varu̍ṇasya̱ śarmopa̍ syāma puru̱vīrā̱ ari̍ṣṭāḥ ||
english: May Aditi, daughter of kings, carry us across all enmities; may Aryaman do so by easy paths. May we abide under the great shelter of Mitra and Varuṇa, rich in heroes, unharmed.

sanskrit: ti̱sro bhūmī̍r dhāraya̱n trīm̐r u̱ta dyūn trīṇi̍ vra̱tā vi̱dathe̍ a̱ntar e̍ṣām | ṛ̱tenā̍dityā̱ mahi̍ vo mahi̱tvaṁ tad a̍ryaman varuṇa mitra̱ cāru̍ ||
english: They sustain three earths and likewise three heavens; three ordinances are established within their assembly. By ṛta, O Ādityas, great is your greatness — that, O Aryaman, Varuṇa, Mitra, is beautiful.

sanskrit: trī ro̍ca̱nā di̱vyā dhā̍rayanta hira̱ṇyayā̱ḥ śuca̍yo̱ dhāra̍pūtāḥ | asva̍pnajo animi̱ṣā ada̍bdhā uru̱śaṁsā̍ ṛ̱jave̱ martyā̍ya ||
english: They sustain the three divine luminous realms; golden are they, pure, cleansed by truth's stream. Unsleeping, unwinking, undeceived, of wide renown — they exist for the protection of the upright mortal.

sanskrit: tvaṁ viśve̍ṣāṁ varuṇāsi̱ rājā̱ ye ca̍ de̱vā a̍sura̱ ye ca̱ martā̍ḥ | śa̱taṁ no̍ rāsva śa̱rado̍ vi̱cakṣe̱ 'śyāmāyū̍ṁṣi̱ sudhi̍tāni̱ pūrvā̍ ||
english: You, O Varuṇa, are king of all — both those gods who are lords of might, and mortals as well. Grant us a hundred autumns that we may see; may we obtain lives well-placed from of old.

sanskrit: na da̍kṣi̱ṇā vi ci̍kite̱ na sa̱vyā na prā̱cīna̍m ādityā̱ nota pa̱ścā | pā̱kyā̍ cid vasavo dhī̱ryā̍ cid yu̱ṣmānī̍to̱ abha̍ya̱ṁ jyoti̍r aśyām ||
english: Neither to the south is it discerned, O Ādityas, nor to the north, neither to the east nor to the west. Even from the wise and the thoughtful, O Vasus — guided by you, may I attain the fearless light.

sanskrit: yo rāja̍bhya ṛta̱nibhyo̍ da̱dāśa̱ yaṁ va̱rdhaya̍nti pu̱ṣṭaya̍ś ca̱ nityā̍ḥ | sa re̱vān yā̍ti pratha̱mo rathe̍na vasu̱dāvā̍ vi̱dathe̍ṣu praśa̱staḥ ||
english: He who has offered to the royal lords of ṛta, whom the perennial abundances make to grow — he, the wealthy one, goes foremost in the chariot, the giver of wealth, praised in the assemblies.

sanskrit: śuci̍r a̱paḥ sū̱yava̍sā̱ ada̍bdha̱ upa̍ kṣeti vṛ̱ddhava̍yāḥ su̱vīra̍ḥ | naki̱ṣ ṭaṁ ghna̱nty anti̍to̱ na dū̱rād ya ā̍di̱tyānā̱m bhava̍ti̱ praṇī̍tau ||
english: Pure, abounding in good pasture, undeceived, he dwells nearby, grown to old age, rich in heroes. None strikes him down, from near or far — he who is under the guidance of the Ādityas.

sanskrit: adi̍te̱ mitra̱ varu̍ṇo̱ta mṛ̍ḻa̱ yad vo̍ va̱yaṁ ca̍kṛ̱mā kac ci̱d āga̍ḥ | u̱rv a̍śyā̱m abha̍ya̱ṁ jyoti̍r indra̱ mā no̍ dī̱rghā a̱bhi na̍śa̱n tami̍srāḥ ||
english: O Aditi, Mitra, Varuṇa, be gracious — whatever transgression we have committed against you. May I attain the wide, fearless light, O Indra; let not the long darkness overcome us.

sanskrit: u̱bhe a̍smai pīpayataḥ samī̱cī di̱vo vṛ̱ṣṭiṁ su̱bhago̱ nāma̱ puṣya̍n | u̱bhā kṣayā̍v ā̱jaya̱n yāti pṛ̱tsūbhāv ardhau̍ bhavataḥ sā̱dhū a̍smai ||
english: Both, meeting together, bestow abundance on him — the rain of heaven, which the fortunate one cherishes by name. He goes conquering both realms in battles; both parties become favorable to him.

sanskrit: yā vo̍ mā̱yā a̍bhi̱druhe̍ yajatrā̱ḥ pāśā̍ ādityā ri̱pave̱ vicṛ̍ttāḥ | a̱śvīva̱ tām̐ ati̍ yeṣa̱ṁ rathe̱nāri̍ṣṭā u̱rāv ā śarma̍n syāma ||
english: Those snares of yours set for the treacherous, O adorable Ādityas, the meshes spread for the enemy — may we pass beyond them like swift horses in a chariot, unharmed, in the wide shelter.

sanskrit: māham ma̱ghono̍ varuṇa pri̱yasya̍ bhūri̱dāvna̱ ā vi̍da̱ṁ śūna̍m ā̱peḥ | mā rā̱yo rā̍jan su̱yamā̱d ava̍ sthām bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: May I not, O Varuṇa, be found bereft of the beloved, bountiful patron's largesse. May we not be set apart from wealth well-governed, O king; may we speak aloud in the assembly, with fine heroes.

sanskrit: i̱daṁ ka̱ver ā̍di̱tyasya̍ sva̱rājo̱ viśvā̍ni̱ sānty a̱bhy a̍stu ma̱hnā | ati̱ yo ma̱ndro ya̱jathā̍ya de̱vaḥ su̍kī̱rtim bhi̍kṣe̱ varu̍ṇasya̱ bhūre̍ḥ ||
english: This is from the seer of Āditya, the self-resplendent sovereign — may it overcome all things with its greatness. He who is the exhilarating god beyond reckoning for worship — I beg the great fame of Varuṇa.

sanskrit: tava̍ vra̱te su̱bhagā̍saḥ syāma svā̱dhyo̍ varuṇa tuṣṭu̱vāṁsa̍ḥ | u̱pāya̍na u̱ṣasā̱ṁ goma̍tīnām a̱gnayo̱ na jara̍māṇā̱ anu̱ dyūn ||
english: In your ordinance may we be blessed and self-sufficient, O Varuṇa, praising you well. Like fires aging through the days, in the coming of the cow-rich Dawns.

sanskrit: tava̍ syāma puru̱vīra̍sya̱ śarma̍nn uru̱śaṁsa̍sya varuṇa praṇetaḥ | yū̱yaṁ na̍ḥ putrā aditer adabdhā a̱bhi kṣa̍madhva̱ṁ yujyā̍ya devāḥ ||
english: May we be in the shelter of you, O Varuṇa, leader, rich in heroes, of wide renown. You, O gods, sons of Aditi, undeceived — govern over us for our companionship.

sanskrit: pra sī̍m ādi̱tyo a̍sṛjad vidha̱rtām̐ ṛ̱taṁ sindha̍vo̱ varu̍ṇasya yanti | na śrā̍myanti̱ na vi mu̍canty e̱te vayo̱ na pa̍ptū raghu̱yā pari̍jman ||
english: Āditya released these who sustain creation; the rivers flow on by Varuṇa's ṛta. They do not weary, nor do they let go — like birds they flew, swift, wheeling around.

sanskrit: vi mac chra̍thāya raśa̱nām i̱vāga̍ ṛ̱dhyāma̍ te varuṇa̱ khām ṛ̱tasya̍ | mā tantu̍ś chedi̱ vaya̍to̱ dhiya̍m me̱ mā mātrā̍ śāry a̱pasa̍ḥ pu̱ra ṛ̱toḥ ||
english: Loosen me, as a rope, from sin; may we prosper at your spring of ṛta, O Varuṇa. Let not the thread be cut while I am weaving; let not the measure be broken before the work is done.

sanskrit: apo̱ su mya̍kṣa varuṇa bhi̱yasa̱m mat samrā̱ḻ ṛtā̱vo 'nu̍ mā gṛbhāya | dāme̍va va̱tsād vi mu̍mu̱gdhy aṁho̍ na̱hi tvad ā̱re ni̱miṣa̍ś ca̱neśe̍ ||
english: Drive fear away from me, O Varuṇa, O sovereign, O upholder of ṛta — seize me not! Like a calf from a rope, loosen the sin from me; for truly I cannot command even the twinkling of an eye without you.

sanskrit: mā no̍ va̱dhair va̍ruṇa̱ ye ta̍ i̱ṣṭāv ena̍ḥ kṛ̱ṇvanta̍m asura bhrī̱ṇanti̍ | mā jyoti̍ṣaḥ pravasa̱thāni̍ ganma̱ vi ṣū mṛdha̍ḥ śiśratho jī̱vase̍ naḥ ||
english: O Varuṇa, let not your missiles that are aimed at the sinner strike us, O mighty one. Let us not depart to the far realms of light; loose our bonds, O gracious one, so that we may live.

sanskrit: nama̍ḥ pu̱rā te̍ varuṇo̱ta nū̱nam u̱tāpa̱raṁ tu̍vijāta bravāma | tve hi ka̱m parva̍te̱ na śri̱tāny apra̍cyutāni dūḻabha vra̱tāni̍ ||
english: Homage to you of old, O Varuṇa, and also now — and again in days to come we shall speak, O mighty-born. For in you, as on a mountain, rest the unshaken, hard-to-attain ordinances.

sanskrit: para̍ ṛ̱ṇā sā̍vī̱r adha̱ matkṛ̍tāni̱ māhaṁ rā̍jann a̱nyakṛ̍tena bhojam | avyu̍ṣṭā̱ in nu bhūya̍sīr u̱ṣāsa̱ ā no̍ jī̱vān va̍ruṇa̱ tāsu̍ śādhi ||
english: Remove the debts that I myself have made, O sovereign; let me not be made to consume what another has committed. Many are the dawns not yet come to light — in those, O Varuṇa, instruct us living ones.

sanskrit: yo me̍ rāja̱n yujyo̍ vā̱ sakhā̍ vā̱ svapne̍ bha̱yam bhī̱rave̱ mahya̱m āha̍ | ste̱no vā̱ yo dipsa̍ti no̱ vṛko̍ vā̱ tvaṁ tasmā̍d varuṇa pāhy a̱smān ||
english: He who is my companion or comrade, O king, or who in a dream tells fear to the fearful like me — whether a thief who plans to betray us, or a wolf — from that one, O Varuṇa, protect us.

sanskrit: māham ma̱ghono̍ varuṇa pri̱yasya̍ bhūri̱dāvna̱ ā vi̍da̱ṁ śūna̍m ā̱peḥ ||
english: May I not, O Varuṇa, be found bereft of the beloved, bountiful patron's largesse. May we not be set apart from wealth well-governed, O king; may we speak aloud in the assembly, with fine heroes.

sanskrit: dhṛta̍vratā̱ ādi̍tyā̱ iṣi̍rā ā̱re mat ka̍rta raha̱sūr i̱vāga̍ḥ | śṛ̱ṇva̱to vo̱ varu̍ṇa̱ mitra̱ devā̍ bha̱drasya̍ vi̱dvām̐ ava̍se huve vaḥ ||
english: The Ādityas, upholders of vows, are swift-moving — keep sin far from me as one keeps a secret wrong at a distance. I, who know the good, call upon you for aid, O Varuṇa, Mitra, gods who are listening.

sanskrit: yū̱yaṁ de̍vā̱ḥ prama̍tir yū̱yam ojo̍ yū̱yaṁ dveṣā̍ṁsi sanu̱tar yu̍yota | a̱bhi̱kṣa̱ttāro̍ a̱bhi ca̱ kṣama̍dhvam a̱dyā ca̍ no mṛ̱ḻaya̍tāpa̱raṁ ca̍ ||
english: You, O gods, are wisdom; you are strength; you are those who ward off enmities from afar. You are the overseers; govern over us — today be gracious to us and also in the future.

sanskrit: kim ū̱ nu va̍ḥ kṛṇavā̱māpa̍reṇa̱ kiṁ sane̍na vasava̱ āpye̍na | yū̱yaṁ no̍ mitrāvaruṇādite ca sva̱stim i̍ndrāmaruto dadhāta ||
english: What shall we do for you anew, O Vasus, or what by the ancient, intimate bond? You, O Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, and Indra and the Maruts — grant us prosperity.

sanskrit: ha̱ye de̍vā yū̱yam id ā̱paya̍ḥ stha̱ te mṛ̍ḻata̱ nādha̍mānāya̱ mahya̍m | mā vo̱ ratho̍ madhyama̱vāḻ ṛ̱te bhū̱n mā yu̱ṣmāva̍tsv ā̱piṣu̍ śramiṣma ||
english: O gods — you indeed are they who must help; be gracious to me who am supplicating. Let not your chariot pass us by in the midst without cause; may we not toil in vain among those who depend on you, among your intimates.

sanskrit: pra va̱ eko̍ mimaya̱ bhūry āgo̱ yan mā̍ pi̱teva̍ kita̱vaṁ śa̍śā̱sa | ā̱re pāśā̍ ā̱re a̱ghāni̍ devā̱ mā mādhi̍ pu̱tre vim i̍va grabhīṣṭa ||
english: I have indeed committed many transgressions — that which a father like a gambler has instructed me in. Far away be the snares, far away the evils, O gods; seize me not in it as a bird in a net.

sanskrit: a̱rvāñco̍ a̱dyā bha̍vatā yajatrā̱ ā vo̱ hārdi̱ bhaya̍māno vyayeyam | trādhva̍ṁ no devā ni̱juro̱ vṛka̍sya̱ trādhva̍ṁ ka̱rtād a̍va̱pado̍ yajatrāḥ ||
english: Turn toward us today, O adorable ones — I, full of fear, would lay open my heart to you. Protect us, O gods, from the ravage of the wolf; protect us from the pit into which one falls, O adorable ones.

sanskrit: māham ma̱ghono̍ varuṇa pri̱yasya̍ bhūri̱dāvna̱ ā vi̍da̱ṁ śūna̍m ā̱peḥ | mā rā̱yo rā̍jan su̱yamā̱d ava̍ sthām bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: May I not, O Varuṇa, be found bereft of the beloved, bountiful patron's largesse. May we not be set apart from wealth well-governed, O king; may we speak aloud in the assembly, with fine heroes.

sanskrit: ṛ̱taṁ de̱vāya̍ kṛṇva̱te sa̍vi̱tra indrā̍yāhi̱ghne na ra̍manta̱ āpa̍ḥ | aha̍r-ahar yāty a̱ktur a̱pāṁ kiyā̱ty ā pra̍tha̱maḥ sarga̍ āsām ||
english: For Savitṛ who makes ṛta, for Indra the serpent-slayer, the waters do not rest. Day after day the ray of the waters passes on; the first flood of them rushes forth.

sanskrit: yo vṛ̱trāya̱ sina̱m atrābha̍riṣya̱t pra taṁ jani̍trī vi̱duṣa̍ uvāca | pa̱tho rada̍ntī̱r anu̱ joṣa̍m asmai di̱ve-di̍ve̱ dhuna̍yo ya̱nty artha̍m ||
english: He who was about to bring destruction here upon Vṛtra — him his mother declared, knowing it. The roaring rivers, breaking the paths in their pleasure, flow day after day to their goal.

sanskrit: ū̱rdhvo hy asthā̱d adhy a̱ntari̱kṣe 'dhā̍ vṛ̱trāya̱ pra va̱dhaṁ ja̍bhāra | miha̱ṁ vasā̍na̱ upa̱ hīm adu̍drot ti̱gmāyu̍dho ajaya̱c chatru̱m indra̍ḥ ||
english: For he stood upright above the mid-region, and thus brought forth his weapon for Vṛtra. Clothed in mist he rushed upon him — Indra, of sharp weapons, conquered the foe.

sanskrit: bṛha̍spate̱ tapu̱ṣāśne̍va vidhya̱ vṛka̍dvaraso̱ asu̍rasya vī̱rān | yathā̍ ja̱ghantha̍ dhṛṣa̱tā pu̱rā ci̍d e̱vā ja̍hi̱ śatru̍m a̱smāka̍m indra ||
english: O Bṛhaspati, pierce like a burning arrow the heroes of the wolf-doored demon. As you slew of old with boldness — even so slay our enemy, O Indra.

sanskrit: ava̍ kṣipa di̱vo aśmā̍nam u̱ccā yena̱ śatru̍m mandasā̱no ni̱jūrvā̍ḥ | to̱kasya̍ sā̱tau tana̍yasya̱ bhūre̍r a̱smām̐ a̱rdhaṁ kṛ̍ṇutād indra̱ gonā̍m ||
english: Hurl down the stone from heaven on high, with which, exhilarated, you crush the foe. In the gaining of offspring and of abundant progeny, let Indra make us the better half of the cows.

sanskrit: pra hi kratu̍ṁ vṛ̱hatho̱ yaṁ va̍nu̱tho ra̱dhrasya̍ stho̱ yaja̍mānasya co̱dau | indrā̍somā yu̱vam a̱smām̐ a̍viṣṭam a̱smin bha̱yasthe̍ kṛṇutam u lo̱kam ||
english: For you carry forth the purpose which you desire to win; you are the stimulators of the poor sacrificer. O Indra and Soma, do you two help us; in this fearful place make for us a world.

sanskrit: na mā̍ tama̱n na śra̍ma̱n nota ta̍ndra̱n na vo̍cāma̱ mā su̍no̱teti̱ soma̍m | yo me̍ pṛ̱ṇād yo dada̱d yo ni̱bodhā̱d yo mā̍ su̱nvanta̱m upa̱ gobhi̱r āya̍t ||
english: Darkness shall not oppress me, nor weariness, nor torpor; we shall not say 'press not the Soma.' He who fills me, who gives, who heeds me, who comes to me when I am pressing with kine.

sanskrit: sara̍svati̱ tvam a̱smām̐ a̍viḍḍhi ma̱rutva̍tī dhṛṣa̱tī je̍ṣi̱ śatrū̍n | tyaṁ ci̱c chardha̍ntaṁ taviṣī̱yamā̍ṇa̱m indro̍ hanti vṛṣa̱bhaṁ śaṇḍi̍kānām ||
english: O Sarasvatī, do you help us; with the Maruts, bold, conquer the enemies. Even that raging, mighty one — Indra slays the bull of the Śaṇḍikas.

sanskrit: yo na̱ḥ sanu̍tya u̱ta vā̍ jigha̱tnur a̍bhi̱khyāya̱ taṁ ti̍gi̱tena̍ vidhya | bṛha̍spata̱ āyu̍dhair jeṣi̱ śatrū̍n dru̱he rīṣa̍nta̱m pari̍ dhehi rājan ||
english: He who from afar or who is about to strike us — look upon him, pierce him with your sharp weapon. O Bṛhaspati, conquer the enemies with your weapons; enclose in a ring the treacherous injurer, O king.

sanskrit: a̱smāke̍bhi̱ḥ satva̍bhiḥ śūra̱ śūrai̍r vī̱ryā̍ kṛdhi̱ yāni̍ te̱ kartvā̍ni | jyog a̍bhūva̱nn anu̍dhūpitāso ha̱tvī teṣā̱m ā bha̍rā no̱ vasū̍ni ||
english: With our warriors, O hero, perform heroic deeds — those which are yours to do. Long may they be scattered as smoke; having slain them, bring us their riches.

sanskrit: taṁ va̱ḥ śardha̱m māru̍taṁ sumna̱yur gi̱ropa̍ bruve̱ nama̍sā̱ daivya̱ṁ jana̍m | yathā̍ ra̱yiṁ sarva̍vīra̱ṁ naśā̍mahā apatya̱sāca̱ṁ śrutya̍ṁ di̱ve-di̍ve ||
english: That host of yours, the Marutas — I who desire their goodwill implore with a hymn and homage the divine folk. That we may daily attain to wealth rich in all heroes, accompanied by offspring, worthy of praise.

sanskrit: a̱smāka̍m mitrāvaruṇāvata̱ṁ ratha̍m ādi̱tyai ru̱drair vasu̍bhiḥ sacā̱bhuvā̍ | pra yad vayo̱ na papta̱n vasma̍na̱s pari̍ śrava̱syavo̱ hṛṣī̍vanto vana̱rṣada̍ḥ ||
english: O Mitra and Varuṇa, protect our chariot together with the Ādityas, the Rudras, the Vasus. When the glory-hungry, exhilarated forest-dwellers flew like birds around the garment.

sanskrit: adha̍ smā na̱ ud a̍vatā sajoṣaso̱ ratha̍ṁ devāso a̱bhi vi̱kṣu vā̍ja̱yum | yad ā̱śava̱ḥ padyā̍bhi̱s titra̍to̱ raja̍ḥ pṛthi̱vyāḥ sānau̱ jaṅgha̍nanta pā̱ṇibhi̍ḥ ||
english: Thus, O gods, willingly do you carry upward our chariot, the prize-seeking one, among the clans. When the swift ones, spreading with their feet, stamped the dust on the ridge of the earth with their hoofs.

sanskrit: u̱ta sya na̱ indro̍ vi̱śvaca̍rṣaṇir di̱vaḥ śardhe̍na̱ māru̍tena su̱kratu̍ḥ ||
english: And may Indra, beholder of all peoples, the wise in purpose, together with the Marutic host of heaven — may he follow close after us with his wolf-like aids for the winning of great wealth in the contest.

sanskrit: u̱ta sya de̱vo bhuva̍nasya sa̱kṣaṇi̱s tvaṣṭā̱ gnābhi̍ḥ sa̱joṣā̍ jūjuva̱d ratha̍m | iḻā̱ bhago̍ bṛhaddi̱vota roda̍sī pū̱ṣā pura̍ṁdhir a̱śvinā̱v adhā̱ patī̍ ||
english: And may Tvaṣṭṛ, the sustainer of existence, together with the wives of the gods in accord, spur on the chariot. Iḷā, Bhaga, Bṛhaddivu, and the two world-halves, Pūṣan, Puraṁdhi, the two Aśvins — they are the lords.

sanskrit: u̱ta tye de̱vī su̱bhage̍ mithū̱dṛśo̱ṣāsā̱naktā̱ jaga̍tām apī̱juvā̍ ||
english: And those two blessed goddesses who behold each other in turn — Dawn and Night, quickeners of the moving world — may I, O Earth, with a fresh utterance praise you; and may all plants that are spreading spring forth from your offspring.

sanskrit: u̱ta va̱ḥ śaṁsa̍m u̱śijā̍m iva śma̱sy ahi̍r bu̱dhnyo̱3̱̍ 'ja eka̍pād u̱ta | tri̱ta ṛ̍bhu̱kṣāḥ sa̍vi̱tā cano̍ dadhe̱ 'pāṁ napā̍d āśu̱hemā̍ dhi̱yā śami̍ ||
english: And we proclaim your praise as do the Uśijs — Ahir Budhnya and Aja Ekapād. Trita, Ṛbhukṣan, Savitṛ has placed his benevolence; Apāṁ Napāt, swift of impulse, has achieved his purpose through prayer.

sanskrit: e̱tā vo̍ va̱śmy udya̍tā yajatrā̱ ata̍kṣann ā̱yavo̱ navya̍se̱ sam | śra̱va̱syavo̱ vāja̍ṁ cakā̱nāḥ sapti̱r na rathyo̱ aha̍ dhī̱tim a̍śyāḥ ||
english: These are those I desire from you, O adorable ones, prepared — which mortal men have fashioned anew together. Like a chariot-horse longing for the prize, O glory-seeker — today may I attain the inspired thought.

sanskrit: a̱sya me̍ dyāvāpṛthivī ṛtāya̱to bhū̱tam a̍vi̱trī vaca̍sa̱ḥ siṣā̍sataḥ | yayo̱r āyu̍ḥ prata̱raṁ te i̱dam pu̱ra upa̍stute vasū̱yur vā̍m ma̱ho da̍dhe ||
english: O Heaven and Earth, be my protectors in ṛta as I seek to win with speech. With whose life-span is longer — those I, who desire wealth, formerly, when praised, have set as great offerings to you both.

sanskrit: mā no̱ guhyā̱ ripa̍ ā̱yor aha̍n dabha̱n mā na̍ ā̱bhyo rī̍radho du̱cchunā̍bhyaḥ | mā no̱ vi yau̍ḥ sa̱khyā vi̱ddhi tasya̍ naḥ sumnāya̱tā mana̍sā̱ tat tve̍mahe ||
english: Let not secret enemies beguile and harm us, let them not injure us with ill omens. Let not the friendship between us be sundered — knowing that, we entreat you with a mind set on goodwill.

sanskrit: ahe̍ḻatā̱ mana̍sā śru̱ṣṭim ā va̍ha̱ duhā̍nāṁ dhe̱num pi̱pyuṣī̍m asa̱ścata̍m | padyā̍bhir ā̱śuṁ vaca̍sā ca vā̱jina̱ṁ tvāṁ hi̍nomi puruhūta vi̱śvahā̍ ||
english: With an unoffending mind bring hearing — the milch cow, swelling inexhaustibly. I urge you, O much-invoked one, each day, with my feet swift in motion and my prize-winning speech.

sanskrit: rā̱kām a̱haṁ su̱havā̍ṁ suṣṭu̱tī hu̍ve śṛ̱ṇotu̍ naḥ su̱bhagā̱ bodha̍tu̱ tmanā̍ | sīvya̱tv apa̍ḥ sū̱cyācchi̍dyamānayā̱ dadā̍tu vī̱raṁ śa̱tadā̍yam u̱kthya̍m ||
english: I invoke Rākā, easy to call, with excellent praise; may the blessed one hear us and awaken of herself. May she sew works together with her needle without missing; may she grant a hero, worthy of praise, the giver of a hundredfold.

sanskrit: yās te̍ rāke suma̱taya̍ḥ su̱peśa̍so̱ yābhi̱r dadā̍si dā̱śuṣe̱ vasū̍ni | tābhi̍r no a̱dya su̱manā̍ u̱pāga̍hi sahasrapo̱ṣaṁ su̍bhage̱ rarā̍ṇā ||
english: O Rākā, those benevolent, well-formed thoughts of yours with which you bestow riches upon the worshipper — with those come to us today, O blessed one, well-disposed, granting thousandfold prosperity.

sanskrit: sinī̍vāli̱ pṛthu̍ṣṭuke̱ yā de̱vānā̱m asi̱ svasā̍ | ju̱ṣasva̍ ha̱vyam āhu̍tam pra̱jāṁ de̍vi didiḍḍhi naḥ ||
english: O Sinīvāli of broad braids, you who are the sister of the gods — accept the oblation that has been offered; O goddess, bestow offspring upon us.

sanskrit: yā su̍bā̱huḥ sva̍ṅgu̱riḥ su̱ṣūmā̍ bahu̱sūva̍rī | tasyai̍ vi̱śpatnyai̍ ha̱viḥ si̍nīvā̱lyai ju̍hotana ||
english: She who has beautiful arms, beautiful fingers, who is kind, mother of many — for her, for the lady of the house, for Sinīvāli, offer the oblation.

sanskrit: yā gu̱ṅgūr yā si̍nīvā̱lī yā rā̱kā yā sara̍svatī | i̱ndrā̱ṇīm a̍hva ū̱taye̍ varuṇā̱nīṁ sva̱staye̍ ||
english: She who is Guṅgū, she who is Sinīvāli, she who is Rākā, she who is Sarasvatī — I call upon Indrāṇī for help, and Varuṇānī for well-being.

sanskrit: ā te̍ pitar marutāṁ su̱mnam e̍tu̱ mā na̱ḥ sūrya̍sya sa̱ṁdṛśo̍ yuyothāḥ | a̱bhi no̍ vī̱ro arva̍ti kṣameta̱ pra jā̍yemahi rudra pra̱jābhi̍ḥ ||
english: O father of the Maruts, may your goodwill come to us; do not keep us away from the sight of the sun. May the hero fare well on his horse; may we be born and multiply in offspring, O Rudra.

sanskrit: tvāda̍ttebhī rudra̱ śaṁta̍mebhiḥ śa̱taṁ himā̍ aśīya bheṣa̱jebhi̍ḥ | vy a1̱̍smad dveṣo̍ vita̱raṁ vy aṁho̱ vy amī̍vāś cātayasvā̱ viṣū̍cīḥ ||
english: With your most healing medicines, O Rudra, with those given by you, may I live a hundred winters. Drive far from us hatred and anguish; ward off diseases in all directions.

sanskrit: śreṣṭho̍ jā̱tasya̍ rudra śri̱yāsi̍ ta̱vasta̍mas ta̱vasā̍ṁ vajrabāho | parṣi̍ ṇaḥ pā̱ram aṁha̍saḥ sva̱sti viśvā̍ a̱bhī̍tī̱ rapa̍so yuyodhi ||
english: You are the most glorious among the born, O Rudra — the mightiest of the mighty, O you of the thunderbolt arm. Carry us beyond distress to well-being; ward off all attacks of injury.

sanskrit: mā tvā̍ rudra cukrudhāmā̱ namo̍bhi̱r mā duṣṭu̍tī vṛṣabha̱ mā sahū̍tī | un no̍ vī̱rām̐ a̍rpaya bheṣa̱jebhi̍r bhi̱ṣakta̍maṁ tvā bhi̱ṣajā̍ṁ śṛṇomi ||
english: Let us not anger you, O Rudra, with our homage; not with ill praise, O bull, not with invocation. Lift up our heroes with your medicines — I hear that you are the most excellent of healers.

sanskrit: havī̍mabhi̱r hava̍te̱ yo ha̱virbhi̱r ava̱ stome̍bhī ru̱draṁ di̍ṣīya | ṛ̱dū̱dara̍ḥ su̱havo̱ mā no̍ a̱syai ba̱bhruḥ su̱śipro̍ rīradhan ma̱nāyai̍ ||
english: He who calls with oblations, him who calls with offerings — with praises I would propitiate Rudra. The tender-bellied, easy to invoke — may the brown, fine-lipped one not harm us, nor our minds.

sanskrit: un mā̍ mamanda vṛṣa̱bho ma̱rutvā̱n tvakṣī̍yasā̱ vaya̍sā̱ nādha̍mānam | ghṛṇī̍va cchā̱yām a̍ra̱pā a̍śī̱yā vi̍vāseyaṁ ru̱drasya̍ su̱mnam ||
english: The bull accompanied by the Maruts has cheered me up, who was supplicating, with swiftly increasing vital strength. Sinless as a shadow in the sun's warmth, I would seek the goodwill of Rudra.

sanskrit: kva1̱̍ sya te̍ rudra mṛḻa̱yāku̱r hasto̱ yo asti̍ bheṣa̱jo jalā̍ṣaḥ | a̱pa̱bha̱rtā rapa̍so̱ daivya̍syā̱bhī nu mā̍ vṛṣabha cakṣamīthāḥ ||
english: Where, O Rudra, is your gracious hand — that which is healing and cooling? O you who remove divine injury — do look upon me, O bull.

sanskrit: pra ba̱bhrave̍ vṛṣa̱bhāya̍ śvitī̱ce ma̱ho ma̱hīṁ su̍ṣṭu̱tim ī̍rayāmi | na̱ma̱syā ka̍lmalī̱kina̱ṁ namo̍bhir gṛṇī̱masi̍ tve̱ṣaṁ ru̱drasya̱ nāma̍ ||
english: To the tawny bull, the white-shining one, I utter great and glorious praise. With reverences we honor the matted one; we proclaim the terrible name of Rudra.

sanskrit: sthi̱rebhi̱r aṅgai̍ḥ puru̱rūpa̍ u̱gro ba̱bhruḥ śu̱krebhi̍ḥ pipiśe̱ hira̍ṇyaiḥ | īśā̍nād a̱sya bhuva̍nasya̱ bhūre̱r na vā u̍ yoṣad ru̱drād a̍su̱rya̍m ||
english: With his firm limbs, of many forms, the fierce and tawny one is adorned with shining gold ornaments. From Rudra who rules this wide existence, divine lordship shall never depart.

sanskrit: arha̍n bibharṣi̱ sāya̍kāni̱ dhanvārha̍n ni̱ṣkaṁ ya̍ja̱taṁ vi̱śvarū̍pam | arha̍nn i̱daṁ da̍yase̱ viśva̱m abhva̱ṁ na vā ojī̍yo rudra̱ tvad a̍sti ||
english: Worthily you bear the arrows and the bow; worthily you wear the neck-ornament worthy of worship, all-formed. Worthily you share out this formidable universe — there is nothing mightier than you, O Rudra.

sanskrit: stu̱hi śru̱taṁ ga̍rta̱sada̱ṁ yuvā̍nam mṛ̱gaṁ na bhī̱mam u̍paha̱tnum u̱gram | mṛ̱ḻā ja̍ri̱tre ru̍dra̱ stavā̍no̱ 'nyaṁ te̍ a̱sman ni va̍pantu̱ senā̍ḥ ||
english: Praise the famous one who sits in the chariot seat, the youthful — terrible and fierce like a wild beast, smiting. Be gracious when praised, O Rudra, to the singer; let your arrows strike down another, not us.

sanskrit: ku̱mā̱raś ci̍t pi̱tara̱ṁ vanda̍māna̱m prati̍ nānāma rudropa̱yanta̍m | bhūre̍r dā̱tāra̱ṁ satpa̍tiṁ gṛṇīṣe stu̱tas tvam bhe̍ṣa̱jā rā̍sy a̱sme ||
english: Even a child bows back to his father when Rudra approaches, to him who comes with reverence. I praise you as the great giver, the true master — you, when praised, give medicines to us.

sanskrit: yā vo̍ bheṣa̱jā ma̍ruta̱ḥ śucī̍ni̱ yā śaṁta̍mā vṛṣaṇo̱ yā ma̍yo̱bhu | yāni̱ manu̱r avṛ̍ṇītā pi̱tā na̱s tā śaṁ ca̱ yoś ca̍ ru̱drasya̍ vaśmi ||
english: Those pure medicines of yours, O Maruts — those most soothing, O bulls, those beneficent ones — those which Manu our father chose — the weal and joy of Rudra I desire.

sanskrit: pari̍ ṇo he̱tī ru̱drasya̍ vṛjyā̱ḥ pari̍ tve̱ṣasya̍ durma̱tir ma̱hī gā̍t | ava̍ sthi̱rā ma̱ghava̍dbhyas tanuṣva̱ mīḍhva̍s to̱kāya̱ tana̍yāya mṛḻa ||
english: May the missile of Rudra pass us by; may the great malevolence of the fierce one pass away. Loosen the rigid ones from the bountiful ones, O liberal giver; be gracious to our offspring and progeny.

sanskrit: e̱vā ba̍bhro vṛṣabha cekitāna̱ yathā̍ deva̱ na hṛ̍ṇī̱ṣe na haṁsi̍ | ha̱va̱na̱śrun no̍ rudre̱ha bo̍dhi bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: Even so, O tawny bull, O wise one, be such, O god, that you do not wroth and do not slay. Hearing our invocations, O Rudra, be gracious here — may we speak aloud in the assembly, with fine heroes.

sanskrit: dhā̱rā̱va̱rā ma̱ruto̍ dhṛ̱ṣṇvo̍jaso mṛ̱gā na bhī̱mās tavi̍ṣībhir a̱rcina̍ḥ ||
english: The Maruts, possessors of rain-streams, of bold might, are terrible as wild beasts in their strengths and shine brightly. Like fires blazing in splendor, impetuous, roaring, they have driven away the cows.

sanskrit: dyāvo̱ na stṛbhi̍ś citayanta khā̱dino̱ vy a1̱̍bhriyā̱ na dyu̍tayanta vṛ̱ṣṭaya̍ḥ | ru̱dro yad vo̍ maruto rukmavakṣaso̱ vṛṣāja̍ni̱ pṛśnyā̍ḥ śu̱kra ūdha̍ni ||
english: Like heavens with stars they shine, the devouring ones; like lightning from the cloud the rains flash forth. When Rudra, O Maruts of golden breastplates, engendered you as the vigorous ones from the bright udder of Pṛśni.

sanskrit: u̱kṣante̱ aśvā̱m̐ atyā̍m̐ ivā̱jiṣu̍ na̱dasya̱ karṇai̍s turayanta ā̱śubhi̍ḥ | hira̍ṇyaśiprā maruto̱ davi̍dhvataḥ pṛ̱kṣaṁ yā̍tha̱ pṛṣa̍tībhiḥ samanyavaḥ ||
english: They anoint themselves like race-horses in the contests, hastening swiftly with the ears of the roaring stream. O golden-helmeted Maruts, gleaming and shaking, you come to the prize with the dappled mares, all of one mind.

sanskrit: pṛ̱kṣe tā viśvā̱ bhuva̍nā vavakṣire mi̱trāya̍ vā̱ sada̱m ā jī̱radā̍navaḥ ||
english: At the prize they have borne all the worlds within them, quick givers, whether ever for Mitra. Dapple-horsed ones of inexhaustible wealth, rushing like hawks in their courses, sitting firmly in the chariot-pole.

sanskrit: indha̍nvabhir dhe̱nubhī̍ ra̱pśadū̍dhabhir adhva̱smabhi̍ḥ pa̱thibhi̍r bhrājadṛṣṭayaḥ | ā ha̱ṁsāso̱ na svasa̍rāṇi gantana̱ madho̱r madā̍ya marutaḥ samanyavaḥ ||
english: With kindling fires, with milch cows of swelling udder, with roads without dust, with shining glances — like swans to their resting-places come, O Maruts of one accord, for the exhilaration of the honey-sweet.

sanskrit: ā no̱ brahmā̍ṇi marutaḥ samanyavo na̱rāṁ na śaṁsa̱ḥ sava̍nāni gantana | aśvā̍m iva pipyata dhe̱num ūdha̍ni̱ kartā̱ dhiya̍ṁ jari̱tre vāja̍peśasam ||
english: Come to our sacred prayers, O Maruts of one accord, as the praise of men to the pressings. Like one who fattens the udder of a milch cow — create for the singer a thought that is shaped by the prize.

sanskrit: taṁ no̍ dāta maruto vā̱jina̱ṁ ratha̍ āpā̱nam brahma̍ ci̱taya̍d di̱ve-di̍ve | iṣa̍ṁ sto̱tṛbhyo̍ vṛ̱jane̍ṣu kā̱rave̍ sa̱nim me̱dhām ari̍ṣṭaṁ du̱ṣṭara̱ṁ saha̍ḥ ||
english: Give us that — the prize-winning one in the chariot, the food that lights up the prayer day by day. Refreshment for the praisers in the enclosures, for the poet — gain, wisdom, inviolability, irresistible might.

sanskrit: yad yu̱ñjate̍ ma̱ruto̍ ru̱kmava̍kṣa̱so 'śvā̱n rathe̍ṣu̱ bhaga̱ ā su̱dāna̍vaḥ | dhe̱nur na śiśve̱ svasa̍reṣu pinvate̱ janā̍ya rā̱taha̍viṣe ma̱hīm iṣa̍m ||
english: When the Maruts of golden breastplates yoke their horses to the chariots in their season, O good givers — like a cow to her calf they swell with abundance in their stations, bestowing great refreshment upon the people who have offered the oblation.

sanskrit: yo no̍ maruto vṛ̱katā̍ti̱ martyo̍ ri̱pur da̱dhe va̍savo̱ rakṣa̍tā ri̱ṣaḥ | va̱rtaya̍ta̱ tapu̍ṣā ca̱kriyā̱bhi tam ava̍ rudrā a̱śaso̍ hantanā̱ vadha̍ḥ ||
english: Whatever mortal enemy sets upon us with wolf-like onslaught, O Vasus, protect us from injury. Turn the fiery wheel-weapon against him; strike him down, O Rudras, with the slaying weapon aimed at the impious.

sanskrit: ci̱traṁ tad vo̍ maruto̱ yāma̍ cekite̱ pṛśnyā̱ yad ūdha̱r apy ā̱payo̍ du̱huḥ | yad vā̍ ni̱de nava̍mānasya rudriyās tri̱taṁ jarā̍ya jura̱tām a̍dābhyāḥ ||
english: Wondrous is that journey of yours, O Maruts, which is celebrated — when the streams milked from Pṛśni's udder. Or when the Rudra-born ones, who are to blame the newly born one, the undeceiving ones, grant Trita to old age to be aged.

sanskrit: tān vo̍ ma̱ho ma̱ruta̍ eva̱yāvno̱ viṣṇo̍r e̱ṣasya̍ prabhṛ̱the ha̍vāmahe | hira̍ṇyavarṇān kaku̱hān ya̱tasru̍co brahma̱ṇyanta̱ḥ śaṁsya̱ṁ rādha̍ īmahe ||
english: Those great Maruts who pass on swiftly we invoke at the advancing of Viṣṇu's step. Golden-hued, lofty, with streaming garments, we who are devoted to prayer seek from them praiseworthy bounty.

sanskrit: te daśa̍gvāḥ pratha̱mā ya̱jñam ū̍hire̱ te no̍ hinvantū̱ṣaso̱ vyu̍ṣṭiṣu | u̱ṣā na rā̱mīr a̍ru̱ṇair apo̍rṇute ma̱ho jyoti̍ṣā śuca̱tā goa̍rṇasā ||
english: They, the ten-fold firstborn, were the first to celebrate the sacrifice; may they impel us at the break of the Dawns. Dawn, like a dark woman, uncovers herself with the ruddy beams of the great, pure light, rich in cows.

sanskrit: te kṣo̱ṇībhi̍r aru̱ṇebhi̱r nāñjibhī̍ ru̱drā ṛ̱tasya̱ sada̍neṣu vāvṛdhuḥ | ni̱megha̍mānā̱ atye̍na̱ pāja̍sā suśca̱ndraṁ varṇa̍ṁ dadhire su̱peśa̍sam ||
english: The Rudras, with their ruddy, unanointed earth-lands, have grown strong in the seats of ṛta. Dripping moisture, with the strength of a steed rushing past, they have assumed a bright complexion, beautiful in form.

sanskrit: tām̐ i̍yā̱no mahi̱ varū̍tham ū̱taya̱ upa̱ ghed e̱nā nama̍sā gṛṇīmasi | tri̱to na yān pañca̱ hotṝ̍n a̱bhiṣṭa̍ya āva̱varta̱d ava̍rāñ ca̱kriyāva̍se ||
english: Seeking those for great shelter and for aid, we approach them indeed with homage and praise. Even as Trita turned the five sacrificial priests downward for the wheel's protection against the oppressor.

sanskrit: yayā̍ ra̱dhram pā̱raya̱thāty aṁho̱ yayā̍ ni̱do mu̱ñcatha̍ vandi̱tāra̍m | a̱rvācī̱ sā ma̍ruto̱ yā va̍ ū̱tir o ṣu vā̱śreva̍ suma̱tir ji̍gātu ||
english: With that aid by which you convey the helpless man beyond distress, by which you free the praiser from the revilers — O Maruts, let that aid of yours turn toward us; may your benevolence come like a lowing cow.

sanskrit: upe̍m asṛkṣi vāja̱yur va̍ca̱syāṁ cano̍ dadhīta nā̱dyo giro̍ me | a̱pāṁ napā̍d āśu̱hemā̍ ku̱vit sa su̱peśa̍sas karati̱ joṣi̍ṣa̱d dhi ||
english: I have been impelled forward, eager for the prize-winning eloquence; may the voice of the rivers rejoice in my hymns. Apāṁ Napāt of swift impulse — will he not render them beautiful and take pleasure in them?

sanskrit: i̱maṁ sv a̍smai hṛ̱da ā suta̍ṣṭa̱m mantra̍ṁ vocema ku̱vid a̍sya̱ veda̍t | a̱pāṁ napā̍d asu̱rya̍sya ma̱hnā viśvā̍ny a̱ryo bhuva̍nā jajāna ||
english: This hymn well-fashioned from the heart — may we speak it; will he come to know it? Apāṁ Napāt, the lord, has by the greatness of his divine lordship generated all the worlds.

sanskrit: sam a̱nyā yanty upa̍ yanty a̱nyāḥ sa̍mā̱nam ū̱rvaṁ na̱dya̍ḥ pṛṇanti | tam ū̱ śuci̱ṁ śuca̍yo dīdi̱vāṁsa̍m a̱pāṁ napā̍ta̱m pari̍ tasthu̱r āpa̍ḥ ||
english: Some waters come together, others flow toward them — the rivers fill the same enclosure. The pure and shining waters have stood around him, Apāṁ Napāt, who is pure and shining.

sanskrit: tam asme̍rā yuva̱tayo̱ yuvā̍nam marmṛ̱jyamā̍nā̱ḥ pari̍ ya̱nty āpa̍ḥ | sa śu̱krebhi̱ḥ śikva̍bhī re̱vad a̱sme dī̱dāyā̍ni̱dhmo ghṛ̱tani̍rṇig a̱psu ||
english: The unwearied young women, the waters, polishing him, the young one, go around him. He of shining and skillful powers shines brightly for us — kindled, clad in ghee, within the waters.

sanskrit: a̱smai ti̱sro a̍vya̱thyāya̱ nārī̍r de̱vāya̍ de̱vīr di̍dhiṣa̱nty anna̍m | kṛtā̍ i̱vopa̱ hi pra̍sa̱rsre a̱psu sa pī̱yūṣa̍ṁ dhayati pūrva̱sūnā̍m ||
english: Three divine women, goddesses, place food for this god without tiring. Constructed, as it were, he has crept forward in the waters; he drinks the first milk of those who gave birth first.

sanskrit: aśva̱syātra̱ jani̍mā̱sya ca̱ sva̍r dru̱ho ri̱ṣaḥ sa̱mpṛca̍ḥ pāhi sū̱rīn | ā̱māsu̍ pū̱rṣu pa̱ro a̍pramṛ̱ṣyaṁ nārā̍tayo̱ vi na̍śa̱n nānṛ̍tāni ||
english: Here is the birthplace of the horse and of the sun; protect the wise ones from the injury of treachery, from mingling with it. In the unripened fortresses, that which cannot be forgotten beyond — may the hostilities vanish, and all falsehoods.

sanskrit: sva ā dame̍ su̱dughā̱ yasya̍ dhe̱nuḥ sva̱dhām pī̍pāya su̱bhv anna̍m atti | so a̱pāṁ napā̍d ū̱rjaya̍nn a̱psv a1̱̍ntar va̍su̱deyā̍ya vidha̱te vi bhā̍ti ||
english: In his own house whose milch cow gives freely, who has drunk up the self-rule and eats wholesome food — that Apāṁ Napāt, energizing within the waters, shines forth for the worshipper for the giving of riches.

sanskrit: yo a̱psv ā śuci̍nā̱ daivye̍na ṛ̱tāvāja̍sra urvi̱yā vi̱bhāti̍ | va̱yā id a̱nyā bhuva̍nāny asya̱ pra jā̍yante vī̱rudha̍ś ca pra̱jābhi̍ḥ ||
english: He who shines widely within the waters with divine purity, an upholder of ṛta inexhaustible — indeed the other worlds and plants with their offspring are born as his branches.

sanskrit: a̱pāṁ napā̱d ā hy asthā̍d u̱pastha̍ṁ ji̱hmānā̍m ū̱rdhvo vi̱dyuta̱ṁ vasā̍naḥ | tasya̱ jyeṣṭha̍m mahi̱māna̱ṁ vaha̍ntī̱r hira̍ṇyavarṇā̱ḥ pari̍ yanti ya̱hvīḥ ||
english: Apāṁ Napāt has stood up in the womb of the recumbent ones, upright, wearing lightning as a garment. Carrying his greatest greatness, the golden-hued, mighty ones go around him.

sanskrit: hira̍ṇyarūpa̱ḥ sa hira̍ṇyasaṁdṛg a̱pāṁ napā̱t sed u̱ hira̍ṇyavarṇaḥ | hi̱ra̱ṇyayā̱t pari̱ yone̍r ni̱ṣadyā̍ hiraṇya̱dā da̍da̱ty anna̍m asmai ||
english: Of golden form is he, of golden appearance — Apāṁ Napāt, he too is golden in color. Sitting within the golden womb, the golden givers give food to him.

sanskrit: tad a̱syānī̍kam u̱ta cāru̱ nāmā̍pī̱cya̍ṁ vardhate̱ naptu̍r a̱pām | yam i̱ndhate̍ yuva̱taya̱ḥ sam i̱tthā hira̍ṇyavarṇaṁ ghṛ̱tam anna̍m asya ||
english: That face of his, and the dear, secret name of Apāṁ Napāt, grows. He whom the young women kindle together in just this way — his food is golden-hued ghee.

sanskrit: a̱smai ba̍hū̱nām a̍va̱māya̱ sakhye̍ ya̱jñair vi̍dhema̱ nama̍sā ha̱virbhi̍ḥ | saṁ sānu̱ mārjmi̱ didhi̍ṣāmi̱ bilmai̱r dadhā̱my annai̱ḥ pari̍ vanda ṛ̱gbhiḥ ||
english: For him, in the friendship of the most lowly of many, we would worship with sacrifices, with homage and oblations. I polish the ridge, I light it with tinder, I place food around it — I honor it with hymns.

sanskrit: sa ī̱ṁ vṛṣā̍janaya̱t tāsu̱ garbha̱ṁ sa ī̱ṁ śiśu̍r dhayati̱ taṁ ri̍hanti | so a̱pāṁ napā̱d ana̍bhimlātavarṇo̱ 'nyasye̍ve̱ha ta̱nvā̍ viveṣa ||
english: He, the bull, engendered the embryo in them; he as an infant sucks from them, they lick him. That Apāṁ Napāt of unfading color has entered here as if with another's body.

sanskrit: a̱smin pa̱de pa̍ra̱me ta̍sthi̱vāṁsa̍m adhva̱smabhi̍r vi̱śvahā̍ dīdi̱vāṁsa̍m | āpo̱ naptre̍ ghṛ̱tam anna̱ṁ vaha̍ntīḥ sva̱yam atkai̱ḥ pari̍ dīyanti ya̱hvīḥ ||
english: Stationed in this highest station, shining everywhere with unstained paths — the great waters, carrying ghee and food to Apāṁ Napāt's grandson, flow around of their own accord with their garments.

sanskrit: ayā̍ṁsam agne sukṣi̱tiṁ janā̱yāyā̍ṁsam u ma̱ghava̍dbhyaḥ suvṛ̱ktim | viśva̱ṁ tad bha̱draṁ yad ava̍nti de̱vā bṛ̱had va̍dema vi̱dathe̍ su̱vīrā̍ḥ ||
english: I have obtained for the people, O Agni, a good dwelling; I have also obtained excellent praise for the bountiful ones. All that is auspicious which the gods protect — may we speak aloud in the assembly, with fine heroes.

sanskrit: tubhya̍ṁ hinvā̱no va̍siṣṭa̱ gā a̱po 'dhu̍kṣan sī̱m avi̍bhi̱r adri̍bhi̱r nara̍ḥ | pibe̍ndra̱ svāhā̱ prahu̍ta̱ṁ vaṣa̍ṭkṛtaṁ ho̱trād ā soma̍m pratha̱mo ya īśi̍ṣe ||
english: Urging for you, O Vasiṣṭha, the men milked the kine and the waters with sheep-wool and pressing-stones. Drink, O Indra, the Soma that has been offered with Svāhā, consecrated with Vaṣaṭ, from the Hotṛ's station — you who as first have the sovereignty.

sanskrit: ya̱jñaiḥ sammi̍ślā̱ḥ pṛṣa̍tībhir ṛ̱ṣṭibhi̱r yāma̍ñ chu̱bhrāso̍ a̱ñjiṣu̍ pri̱yā u̱ta | ā̱sadyā̍ ba̱rhir bha̍ratasya sūnavaḥ po̱trād ā soma̍m pibatā divo naraḥ ||
english: Mingled with the sacrifices and with the dappled mares and spears, beautiful in their anointing on the path, and dear — O sons of Bharata, having taken your seat on the sacred grass, O men of heaven, drink the Soma from the Potṛ's station.

sanskrit: a̱meva̍ naḥ suhavā̱ ā hi ganta̍na̱ ni ba̱rhiṣi̍ sadatanā̱ raṇi̍ṣṭana | athā̍ mandasva jujuṣā̱ṇo andha̍sa̱s tvaṣṭa̍r de̱vebhi̱r jani̍bhiḥ su̱madga̍ṇaḥ ||
english: Come near to us like a friend, easy to invoke; sit down upon the sacred grass and rejoice. Then be exhilarated, taking pleasure in the drink, O Tvaṣṭṛ, with the gods and with the divine women, in their company.

sanskrit: ā va̍kṣi de̱vām̐ i̱ha vi̍pra̱ yakṣi̍ co̱śan ho̍ta̱r ni ṣa̍dā̱ yoni̍ṣu tri̱ṣu | prati̍ vīhi̱ prasthi̍taṁ so̱myam madhu̱ pibāgnī̍dhrā̱t tava̍ bhā̱gasya̍ tṛpṇuhi ||
english: Bring hither the gods, O inspired Hotṛ — sacrifice, eager one; sit down in the three stations. Fill in return the onward-moving soma-honey; drink from the Agnīdh's station; satisfy yourself with your own share.

sanskrit: e̱ṣa sya te̍ ta̱nvo̍ nṛmṇa̱vardha̍na̱ḥ saha̱ oja̍ḥ pra̱divi̍ bā̱hvor hi̱taḥ ||
english: This is that which increases the manly strength of your body, the might placed from of old in your two arms. O bountiful one, it has been pressed for you and brought to you — you yourself, O Indra, drink to satisfaction from the Brahman's station.

sanskrit: ju̱ṣethā̍ṁ ya̱jñam bodha̍ta̱ṁ hava̍sya me sa̱tto hotā̍ ni̱vida̍ṁ pū̱rvyā anu̍ | acchā̱ rājā̍nā̱ nama̍ ety ā̱vṛta̍m praśā̱strād ā pi̍bataṁ so̱myam madhu̍ ||
english: Take pleasure in the sacrifice, both of you; hearken to my call. The Hotṛ, having sat down, recites the nivid following the ancient formula. Homage goes toward the two kings who turn hither — from the Praśāstr's station, drink the soma-honey.
